parties:
Bank Asia Limited ---------- Petitioner
Vs.
Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Chattogram and others ---------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ashfaqul Islam J : This Rule at the instance of Bank Asia Limited, issued on 22-5-2017, was in the following terms:

"Let A Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why it should not be declared that after the issuance of the certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 vide order No. 20 dated 19-8-2015 the Artha Jari Mamla No. 76 of 2013 of the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong was finally disposed of and the executing court became functus officio and as to why the impugned order No. 35 dated 2-1-2017 and its subsequent extension order No. 38 dated 26-1-2017 and order No. 40 dated 1-2-2017 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Artha Jari Mamla No. 76 of 2013 staying further proceedings relating to the kabala No. 19296 dated 29-12-2016 and the delivery of possession thereunder shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

Pending hearing of the Rule, let operation of the impugned orders passed in Artha Jari Mamla No. 76 of 2013 now pending before the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong be stayed for a period of 3 months from date."

2. The averments figured in the petition, leading to the Rule, in short are that the petitioner is a Banking Company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994 and involved in Banking Business. The decree holder-petitioner-Bank as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 4 of 2012 on 16-1-2012 in the Court of the Artha Rin Adalat (hereinafter referred to as Adalat), Chittagong against the Judgment debtors-respondents No. 2-5 herein as defendants Nos. 1-4 for realization of the outstanding loan liabilities of the defendants, contending, inter-alia, that the borrower-defendants have been enjoying credit facilities in the form of Letter of Credit (L/C) Loan against Trust Receipts (LTR) and Overdraft (OD) sanctioned by the plaintiff bank and that subsequently the borrower-defendants failed to pay off their loan liability for which the plaintiff bank instituted the said Artha Rin Suit No. 4 of 2012, against the said borrower defendants.

3. The Judgment debtor-respondents herein as defendants contested the said suit by filling written statement on 5-6-2012 denying all the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the defendants have settled the entire loan amount of the plaintiff Bank but it has filed the suit obtaining unlawful gain. Upon hearing the parties the Court of Joint District Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong decreed the suit with a direction upon the defendants to pay the said amount within 60 days failing which the decree holder Bank can recover the same by filing the execution case.

4. The respondents Nos. 2-5 (defendants) having failed to pay the decretal amount within time the decree holder petitioner Bank put the said decree into execution on 27-11-2013 in Artha Jari Mamla No. 76 of 2013 before the Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong for recovery of decretal amount by selling the mortgaged properties. In the said Artha Jari Mamla the mortgaged property of the Judgment-debtors was tried to be sold in auction through court on 20-4-2015 and 8-7-2015 but it could not be sold for want of suitable bidder. The decree holder-petitioner-Bank then on 19-8-2015 filed an application under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for issuance of a certificate in its favour for selling the mortgaged property and the Adalat vide its Order No. 20 dated 19-8-2015 was pleased to allow the said application and issued the Certificate on 19-8-2015 (Annexure-"B").

5. In pursuance of the certificate issued under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as Ain) the decree holder-petitioner-Bank auction sold 1 mortgaged property out of the total 5 mortgaged properties for an amount of Taka 7,02,20,777 vide Sale Deed No. 19296 dated 29-12-2016 to the proforma-respondent No. 6, the auction purchaser. On an off date on 2-1-2017 the Judgment debtors-respondents No. 2-5 herein filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure with prayer to cancel the said deed of sale No. 19296 dated 29-12-2016 with a further prayer under section 94(e) of the Code of Civil Procedure read with section 44 and 57 of the Artha Rin Ain Adalat, 2003 to restrain the decree holder-Petitioner-Bank herein from making delivery of possession thereof. The Adalat its impugned Order No. 35 dated 2-1-2017 passed in Artha Jari Mamla No. 76 of 2013 on an off date was pleased to stay the further proceedings relating to the said Kabala No. 19296 dated 29-12-2016 and the delivery of possession thereunder and subsequently extended the same vide orders Nos. 38 dated 26-1-2017 and Order No. 40 dated 1-2-2017 (Annexure-"D").

6. It is at this stage the petitioner moved this division and obtained the present Rule and order of stay.

7. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mrs. Shahnaj Akther the learned Advocate for the petitioner after placing the petition, the impugned order and other materials on records advanced following arguments:- Having regard to the fact that in the Artha Jari Mamla No. 76 of 2013 the certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as Ain) was issued on 19-8-2015 by the Executing Court in favour of the decree holder-petitioner-Bank for possession, enjoyment and transfer of the mortgaged land and in pursuance thereof the decree holder-petitioner-Bank auction sold one of the said mortgaged land vide kabala No. 19296 dated 29-12-2016 and as such the said Artha jari Mamla No. 76 of 2013 was disposed of finally, consequently the Executing Court had no jurisdiction to entertain the application dated 2-1-2017 filed by the judgment debtors-respondents and to pass thereon the impugned orders staying further proceedings relating to the said kabala No. 19296 dated 29-12-2016 and the delivery of possession thereunder and as such the impugned orders are illegal, without lawfully authority and are of no legal effect.

8. In elaborating his submissions the learned counsel further contends that it is established principle of law that after issuance of the certificate under section 33(5) and/or section 33(7) of the Ain in respect of the mortgaged property in favour of the decree holder-Bank the execution case arising thereunder is finally disposed of in satisfaction of the decree and the executing court becomes functus officio, consequently the respondent No. 1, the Adalat acted illegally, without jurisdiction and without lawful authority in entertaining the respondents-Judgment debtors' application dated 2-1-2017 and passing the impugned order thereon long after the issuance of the certificate on 19-8-2015 under section 33(5) of the Ain in favour of the decree holder-petitioner-bank.

9. In support of his contention the learned counsel placed reliance in the decision of Sk. Mohiuddin vs Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka 13 MLR (AD) 356, Sonali Bank vs Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj 15 MLR (AD) 20 = 62 DLR (AD) 231, Sheuly Khanam vs Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka 17 BLC 579 (where one of us was a party) and Feroza Begum vs Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka 36 BLD (AD) 31.

10. Respondent No. 6, who is the auction purchaser by filling affidavit-in-opposition supports the Rule.

11. The learned Counsel Mr Shamim Khaled appearing for the respondent No. 6 adopted the arguments placed by the petitioner as aforesaid and reiterated that after issuance of certificate under sections 33(5) or 33(7) of the Ain read with section 33(9) of the Ain, the court became functus officio subject to section 28 of the Ain.

12. In General, it is accepted proposition of law that with the issuance of certificate under sections 33(5) and 33(7) the court becomes functus officio since the execution case has been finally disposed of but subject to section 28. In other words, it can be said that only for the purpose of limitation in filing execution cases section 28 comes into play with all it's trappings.

13. None appears to oppose the Rule on behalf of the respondent defendant.

14. We have heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and the auction purchaser respondent No. 6 at length and considered their submissions carefully.

15. Only question for determination in the instant writ petition is whether under the facts and circumstance and the relevant laws applicable on the issue, the executing court acted without jurisdiction in passing the order impugned against.

16. To appreciate the issue and for better understanding let us first glean what the relevant law enjoins, section 33(5):

৩৩ (৫) কোন সম্পত্তি উপ-ধারা (১), (২), ২(ক), (২খ), (২গ), (৩) ও (8) এর বিধান অনুসারে বিক্রয় করা সম্ভব না হইলে, উক্ত সম্পত্তি, ডিক্রীকৃত দাবী পরিপূর্ণভাবে  পরিশোধিত না হওয়া পর্যন্ত, দখল ও ভোগের অধিকারসহ ও ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত করা হইবে, এবং ডিক্রীদার উপ-ধারা (১), (২), (২ক), (২খ), (২গ), (৩) ও (8) এর বিধান অনুসারে উক্ত সম্পত্তি বিক্রয় করিয়া অপরিশোধিত ডিক্রীর দাবী আদায় করিতে পারিবে, এবং আদালত এ মর্মে একটি

সার্টিফিকেট ইস্যু করিবে।

(৬)-------------

৬(ক)------------

৬(খ)------------

(৭) উপ-ধারা (8) ও (৫) এর বিধান সত্বেও, ডিক্রীদার, উল্লিখিত সম্পত্তি মালিকানাসত্ত্বে পাইতে আগ্রহী মর্মে আদালতের নিকট লিখিতভাবে আবেদন করিলে, আদালত, উপ-ধারা (১), (২), (২ক), (২খ), (২গ), (৩) এর বিধানাবলীর কোনররূপ হানি না ঘটাইয়া, উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর কার্যক্রম অনুসরণ করা হইতে বিরত থাকিবে; এবং ডিক্রীদারের প্রার্থিতমতে উল্লেখিত সম্পত্তির স্বত্ত্ব ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত হইয়াছে মর্মে ঘোষণা প্রদানপূর্বক তৎমর্মে একটি

সনদপত্র জারি করিবে এবং জারীকৃত এইরূপ সনদপত্র স্বত্ত্বের দলিল হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে; এবং আদালত উহার একটি অনুলিপি সংশ্লিষ্ট স্থানীয় সাব-রেজিষ্টারের অফিসে নিবন্ধনের জন্য প্রেরণ করিবে।

৭(ক)-------------

৭(খ)------------

(৮)------------

(৯) উপ-ধারা (৫) এর অধীনে সম্পত্তির দখল ও ভোগের অধিকার অথবা উপ-ধারা (৭) এর অধীনে সম্পত্তির ডিত্রীদারের স্বত্ত্ব অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত হইলে, ধারা ২৮ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, উক্ত ডিক্রী জারি মামলার চূড়ান্ত নিষ্পত্তি হইবে ।

17. Further it is very important to quote section 33(7)05) and 7(10 in this regard. Section 33(7)() and 7(4) runs as under:

৩৩৫৭)কে) উপ-ধারা (৫) বা (৭) এর অধীন সম্পত্তির দখল আদালতযোগে প্রাপ্ত হওয়া আবশ্যক হইলে, ডিক্রীদারের লিখিত আবেদনের ভিত্তিতে আদালত ডিক্রীদারকে উক্ত সম্পত্তির দখল অর্প্ন করিতে পারিবে ।

৭(খ) উপ-ধারা (৭ক) এর অধীন ডিভ্রীদারকে সম্পত্তির দখল অর্প্ন করিবার পূর্বে আদালতকে পুনঃ নিশ্চিত হইতে হইবে যে, উক্ত সম্পত্তিই আইনানুগভাবে উহার প্রকৃত মালিক কর্তৃক ডিক্রীর সংশ্লিষ্ট ঋনের বিপরীতে বন্ধক প্রদান করা হইয়াছিল অথবা ডিক্রী কার্য্কর করিবার লক্ষ্যে দায়িকের প্রকৃত স্বত্ত্ব দখলীয় সম্পত্তি হিসাবে উক্ত সম্পত্তিই ক্রোক করা হইয়াছিল।

18. This 7(ক) and 7(খ) of section 33 was inserted in the year of 2010 (law No. 16 of 2010). Before this amendment, in 13 MLR (AD) 356 case our Appellate Division observed the legal consequence of the issuance of certificate under sections 33(5) and 33(7) read with 33(9) of the Ain which was also applied in the decision of Sheuly Khanam's case 17 BLC as referred to above (where one of us was a party). Their lordships of the Appellate Division in 13 MLR case repelled the argument of the learned Counsel for the petitioner in that case Mr AJ Mohammad Ali and observed the followings:

"Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, the learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the certificate issued under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in favour of the decree-holder bank is only for possession and enjoyment of the mortgaged property and it did not mean final disposal of the Execution case for which further action for disposal of the suit property is necessary under section 33(7) of the said Act, but the High Court Division misconducted the provision of section 33(9) in holding that the Execution case was finally disposed of and thereby erred in summarily rejecting the writ petition. He lastly submits that the decree being in preliminary form, the suit remained pending and thus the Artha Rin Adalat had the jurisdiction to consider the application for stay under section 44 of the Act and to grant installment payment under section 49 of the Act, but the Artha Rin Adalat failed to exercise its jurisdiction on the erroneous view of law that it became functus officio and had no jurisdiction to decide the application on merit.

We have heard the learned Advocate and perused the connected papers including the impugned judgment. We do not find any substance in the points raised. The High Court Division upon correct assessment of the legal position and materials on record arrived at a correct decision. We therefore, find no reason to interfere with the same."

<u>19. The same principle echoed in 17 BLC case. 13 MLR Appellate Division case was delivered on March 27, 2008 and 17 BLC decision of this Division was delivered on 27th February, 2012. Thus, when the Appellate Division gave verdict in 13 MLR case, section 33(7)(ক) and 7(খ) were not there but when subsequent decision of 17 BLC:s Case came in February 2012, Provisions of 33(7)(ক) and 7(খ) of the Ain came into force by amendment of 2010. However, In Firoza Begum's case 36 BLD finally our Appellate Division held the same view that after issuance of certificate under 33(5) the execution case is disposed of finally and the executing court becomes functus officio under section 33(9) and as such executing court cease to have any jurisdiction to entertain the judgment debtor's application for cancellation of auction sale. The same principle after amendment in the year 2010 has been further reiterated by the Appellate Division in 15 MLR case as referred to above in the following manner:—</u>

<u>"It appears that the leave petitioner bank is negligent in not informing the executing court about the fact of restoration of the Rule and stay dated 15-6-2006 and that the leave petitioner bank by filing an application on 25-6-2006 prayed for receiving the pay order submitted by the auction purchaser in Court and it appears from the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division that the leave petitioner bank has already encashed the pay order and thereby accepted the auction sale. In view of the provision of law to the effect that once an auction sale is complete no relief is available against such auction sale but the mortgage may proceed against the mortgagor-bank for any compensation, if it is proved that there was illegality in the auction sale. In the instant case, it is not such case rather it appears that at the instance of the decree-holder-bank auction was held and ultimately the decree holder-bank has withdrawn the money deposited by the auction purchasers. After the auction process is completed, proceedings with the execution case is redundant.</u>

<u>20. On a plain reading of section 33(7)(ক) and 7(খ) of the Ain, it appears that the provisions do not have any bearing or so to say it cannot circumvent the principle as it has been laid down by both the Divisions time and again. The contradictory decisions as it could be found in IFIC Bank's case 15 BLT 425 and Salma Begum's case 63 DLR does not apply in the instant case at all. Therefore, we certainly find merit and substance in the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that with the granting of certificate under section 33(5) or 33(7) of the Ain the Execution Case is finally disposed of and the executing court becomes functus officio.</u>

21. In the result the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The decision taken by the order impugned against No. 35 dated 2-1-2017 and its subsequent extension Order No. 38 dated 26-1-2017 and Order No. 40 dated 1-2-2017 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat Chittagong in Artha Jari Mamla No. 76 of 2013 staying further proceedings relating to the kabala No.19296 dated 29-12-2016 are declared to have been passed without lawful authority having no legal effect and accordingly set aside.

Communicate at once.

End.

lawyer:
Dr KM Hafizul Alam Hafiz with SM Bazlur Rashid with Humayun Kabir Sikder, Advocates—For the Petitioner. 

Rabeya Bhuiyan with Mr Mahmood Morshed with Saleh Akram, Advocates—For the Opposite-Parties.
parties:
Farzana Sharmin Hossain ----------- Plaintiff-Appellant-Petitioner
Vs. 
Md Shakhawat Hossain and others -------- Defendant-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
At the instance of the present plaintiff-appellant-petitioner, Mrs Farzana Sharmin Hossain, this Rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 5-4-2017 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th court, Dhaka in Family Appeal No. 156 of 2016 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 6-6-2016 passed by the 2nd Additional Assistant Judge and Family Court, Dhaka in Family Suit No. 486 of 2016 rejecting the application under section 16A of the Family Court Ordinance, 1985 should not be set-aside.

2. The relevant facts for disposal of this Rule, inter-alia, are that the present petitioner Mrs Farzana Sharmin Hossain as the plaintiff filed the Family Suit No. 326 of 2016 which was renumbered as the Family Suit No. 486 of 2016 in the court of learned Additional Assistant Judge and Family Court, court No. 2, Dhaka for declaration that the divorce notice dated 20-3-2016 and the Arbitration Case No. 124 of 2016 filed in the Dhaka South City Corporation was not maintainable as per law. In the said suit, the present-petitioner filed an application for an injunction upon the proceeding of the said arbitration case filed under section 16A of the Family Court Ordinance, 1985 restraining the present-defendant-opposite party No.1 from another marriage and notice to become in-operative.

3. The plaint case is that the present-opposite party No.1 and the petitioner had solemnized their marriage on 10-9-1999 by registering a Nikahnama and fixing Taka 5,00,001 (Taka Five Lacs one) only as dower money. During their wedlock three children were born being Sazid Shafwat Hossain (now aged about 16 years), daughter Ifrit Nahian Hossain aged about 15 years, and another son Samid Shafwat Hossain aged about 9 years. The petitioner further claims that their family life had been very happy with the above three children. The petitioner noticed some unusual conducts of the present-opposite party No.1 as her husband because of the instigations from other family members and some immoral physical relationship with others. She then filed Family Suit No. 486 of 2016 of her conjugal right which is pending in the concerned court. The defendant No.1 served a notice dated 20-3-2016 for divorcing the petitioner as his wife and also served the same notice to the Dhaka South City Corporation as per the provision of law. Accordingly, the Arbitration Case No. 124 of 2016 was initiated by the Dhaka South City Corporation with an intention for reconciliation between the parties as per law. While the said case was proceeding different dates were fixed for hearing of the parties as per necessary steps required as per provision of Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961. During the pendency of the said case the present-petitioner filed the Family Suit No. 326 of 2016. The suit is pending for disposal. During the pendency of the said suit the present-petitioner field an application for staying the operation of the divorce notice dated 20-3-2016 from which the Arbitration Case No. 124 of 2016 arose. The said application was filed on the ground that on 17-6-2016 the present-opposite party No.1 came to the house of the present-petitioner and they had a physical relationship as husband and wife which has revoked the divorce notice dated 20-3-2016.

4. After considering the submissions made by the learned Advocates appearing of the respective parties the said application was rejected on 6-6-2016 by the learned trial court. Being aggrieved the present-petitioner as the appellant preferred the Family Appeal No. 156 of 2016 in the court of the learned District Judge, Dhaka who by his judgment and order dated 26-6-2016 admitted the appeal and also passed the impugned order of stay upon all further proceedings of the Arbitration Case No. 124 of 2016 until further order and also transferred the appeal to the court of learned Additional District Judge, 5th court, Dhaka, who after hearing the parties dismissed the appeal by his judgment and order dated 5-4-2017. This revisional application has been filed under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the legality of the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned appellate court and the present Rule was issued thereupon.

5. Dr Hafijul Alam Hafiz, the learned Advocate, appearing along with the learned Advocates Mr. Humayun Kabir Sikder, Mr SM Bazlur Rashid, and Mr Utfal Kumar Saha for the petitioner, submits that the courts below failed to consider the facts and circumstances that the defendant-opposite party No.1 came to the house of the plaintiff-petitioner and had a sexual intercourse within the period of 90 days from sending the notice under section 7 of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961, as such, the courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, as such, the Rule should be made absolute.

6. The learned Advocate also submits that the provision under the Mohammedan Law physical contact between the parties revokes any divorce notice impliedly, as such, the arbitration proceeding in the Dhaka South City Corporation cannot be a valid proceeding until a fresh divorce notice is served by the husband to the wife, as such, the Rule should be made absolute.

7. The Rule has been opposed by the present- opposite party No. 1.

8. Mrs Rabeya Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Counsel appearing along with the learned Advocate Mr Mahmood Morshed, and Mr. Shaleh Akram for the opposite parties, submits that the divorce notice dated 20-3-2016 was served by the present-Opposite party No.1 as the husband upon the present-petitioner, wife and also to the concerned authorities including Dhaka South City Corporation as per the provision of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961, accordingly, the Arbitration Case No. 124 of 2016 was initiated and concluded by the Executive Arbitration Council Officer and Local Executive Officer, Anchal-1, Dhaka South City Corporation on 2-5-2017, therefore, any ad-interim order of stay cannot be passed for staying the arbitration proceeding, as such, the Rule should be discharged.

<u>9. The learned Advocate further submits that section 3 of the Ordinance, 1961 is an overriding provision of law which overrides even the Sharia Law, Customs and Uses under the Muslim Family Law, therefore, a divorce notice by a husband to the wife under section 7(1) of the said Ordinance, 1961 cannot be stayed unless and until the parties jointly revoke or withdrawn the arbitration proceeding by joint prayer within the period of 90 days, thus, the Arbitration Council has no other alternative but to declaration divorce final but the present-petitioner obtained the present Rule by misleading this court which is liable to be discharged.</u>

10. Considering the above submissions made by the learned Advocates appearing for the respective parties and also considering the revisional application filed under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure along with the Annexures therein and also considering the Supplementary-affidavit and Counter-affidavit filed by the respective parties, it appears to me that the present-petitioner and the opposite party No.1 married on 10-9-1999 and there are three children in their family. The present-petitioner (wife) noticed some unusual conducts or acts of her husband in the year of 2016, including, engaging into some illicit relations with others at the instigation from his family members. The admitted position between the parties is that they were married and they have three children. However, there are some disputes as to the effectiveness of a divorce proceeding initiated by the present-opposite party No.1 (husband) by serving a divorce talaknama notice through the Kazi Office under section 7(1) of the Ordinance, 1961. The present-petitioner served the said notice on 20-3-2016 and the Dhaka South City Corporation initiated the proceeding on 13-4-2016. Before conclusion of the said steps of the divorce proceeding the present-petitioner filed the suit on 5-6-2016 for declaring the divorce proceeding illegal and not binding upon her.

11. In the above given factual as facts in this case, this Court has to take a decision whether the courts below committed any error of law by passing the concurrent decision rejecting the prayer to stay the divorce proceeding continuing in the Arbitration Case No. 124 of 2016 before the Arbitration Council under the City Corporation. In order to take a decision upon the said matter, I have carefully examined the impugned judgment and order passed by the courts below along with other relevant documents submitted by the respective parties. I have also considered the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985 and also the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961. The above Ordinances deal with a divorce proceeding as well as the proceeding for the divorce purpose. Section 7 of the Ordinance, 1961 reads as follows:

7. Talaq—(1) Any man who wishes to divorce his wife shall, as soon as may be after the pronouncement of talaq in any form whatsoever, give the Chairman notice in writing of his having done so, and shall supply a copy thereof to the wife.

12. As per the above provision of law, the present-opposite party No.1 served a divorce notice on 20-3-2016 and follows all the steps as per the above law. However, the present-petitioner filed the suit challenging the legality of the said divorce notice on the ground that there was a break of notice within 90 days period for conclusion of the divorce proceeding by way of having a sexual relationship between them on 17-6-2016. In this regard I consider that such kind of physical contact was simply an emotional conduct in ignorance of a legal procedures which a court of law cannot take into consideration because a statutory stipulated period of time and manner.

13. In this regard section 7(3) and (5) of the Ordinance describes any lawful revocation of any divorce proceeding which reads as follows:—

"(3) Save as provided in sub-section (5), a talaq, unless revoked earlier, expressly or otherwise, shall not be effective until the expiration of ninety days from the day on which notice under sub-section (1) is delivered to the Chairman.

(5) If the wife be pregnant at the time talaq is pronounced, talaq shall not be effective until the period mentioned in sub-section 2[(3)] or the pregnancy, whichever be later, ends."

14. In view of the above provision of law, a divorce proceeding can only be interrupted or even revoked by the order of the Arbitration Council on the joint prayer of both the husband and wife on consent or by the divorce notice serving party to withdraw the proceeding after reconciliation between the parties. In the instant case, the present- opposite party No.1 served the divorce notice and there is no evidence before this Court that he withdraw the divorce proceeding in order to reconciliation. Therefore, the suit filed by the present-petitioner, the learned trial court would take a final conclusion of the suit on merit after hearing the parties. Regarding this ad-interim order of stay of a proceeding is not a permissible by any party other then the parties concerned through the arbitration proceeding in the Arbitration Council. As such, 90 days period of the reconciliation is a final period of revocation of any divorce notice. In view of the above, I do not consider that the learned appellate court committed any error of law by concurrently finding against the present-petitioner as the applicant for staying proceeding of the divorce notice by any ad- interim order of stay. However, the learned trial court would dispose of the Family Suit No. 326 of 2016, which was renumbered as Family Suit No. 486 of 2016 on merit after giving the sufficient opportunities to both the parties for producing relevant evidence.

15. 1 am of the view that the statutory provision of section 7 under the Ordinance, 1961 overrides any other Provision of law or even Customs or Uses or Practice, therefore, any such relation between the parties would be considered by the learned trial court after examining evidence adduced and produced by the parties in the trial court, but, any ad-interim order of stay would not be granted which could delay the disposal of the Family Suit No. 486 of 2016 pending in the court of learned Additional Assistant Judge and Family Court No. 2, Dhaka.

16. In view of the above, I have considered the findings of the learned appellate court who concurrently lawfully dismissed the appeal preferred by the present-petitioner on the basis of the following finding:—

প্রকৃতপক্ষে সালিশী পরিষদের কার্য্ক্রমের উপর স্থগিতাদেশ কার্য্কর না থাকলে এতদিনে তালাক কার্য্কর হয়ে যেত। যদিও চেয়ারম্যান নোটিশ প্রাপ্ত হওয়ার ৯০ দিন অতিবাহিত হয়েছে এবং সেমতে বাদী ও বিবাদীর মধ্যে তালাক কার্য্কর হয়েছে মর্মে প্রতীয়মান হয়। কাজেই আপীলকারী পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ কৌসুলীর উপরে উল্লেখিত দাবী যুক্তিযুক্ত ও আইনানুগ নয়।

17. On the basis of the above discussions and after perusal of the impugned judgment and order I consider that the learned appellate court committed no error of law by dismissing the appeal concurrently. I am, therefore, not inclined to interfere into the judgment and order passed by the learned appellate court.

18. Accordingly, I do not find merit in the Rule.

19. In the result, the Rule is discharged with the following direction.

20. The learned Additional Assistant Judge; 2nd Court, Dhaka and Family Court, Dhaka is hereby directed to conclude the Family Suit No. 486 of 2016 previously the Family Suit No. 326 of 2016 within 2(two) months from the date of receipt of this judgment and order of this Court without allowing any unnecessary adjournment on the prayer of the either of the parties.

21. The ad-interim order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated.

The office is directed to communicate the judgment and order to the concern court immediately.

End.

parties:
Mustafa Kamal Akhter  and others --------- Petitioners
VS
Salema Khatun and others --------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-10 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 6-4-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Second Commercial Court, Chittagong in Other Appeal No. 701 of 1991 reversing the judgment and decree dated 25-9-1991 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, First Additional Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 41 of 1991 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the predecessor of opposite party, Salema Khatun as plaintiff instituted Other Suit No. 105 of 1989 subsequently, renumbered as Other Suit No. 41 of 1991 against the present petitioner and pro forma opposite party No. 11 as defendant for declaration of title by way of gift and adverse possession stating that the property in question belonged to one Nawab Ali, husband of the plaintiff who by a deed of gift dated 6-7-1969 gifted the suit land to the plaintiff and by other registered deeds of gift said Nawab Ali gifted his other landed property to his other heirs. Nawab Ali had four wives, the plaintiff is the second wife. Nawab Ali gifted some non-suited property to his son defendant No. 8, Md Muslim, but in the said deed of gift the deed writer wrongly included the suit property already gifted to the plaintiff. After making the gift by Nawab Ali in favour of the plaintiff, the plaintiff got delivery of possession, but for long time the plaintiff had no knowledge about inclusion of her gifted property in the deed of gift made by Nawab Ali in favour of his minor son Md Muslim. In fact the suit property never gifted to defendant No. 8, Muslim and Nawab Ali never expressed his willingness to make gift of the suit property in favour of Md Muslim.

The plaintiff have been possessing the suit land with the knowledge of all. The defendant never possessed the same but in the last part of 1987, father of defendant Nos. 1-7 with some unknown people came to the suit land and threatened the plaintiff with dispossession claiming that they purchased the property from defendant No. 8, Md Muslim, though, they did not acquire any title and possession in the suit property by the alleged purchase, hence, the suit for declaration of title.

3. Defendant Nos. 1-3 and 5-7 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form; the suit is barred by limitation and it has no cause of action. It was also alleged that the suit has not been filed by the plaintiff but it is filed by putting thumb impression of her son Mahbub. The suit property was gifted by Nawab Ali in favour of his son Md Muslim by deed of gift No. 4073 dated 6-7-1969 and delivered possession of the same to him. The said Md Muslim while in possession and enjoyment of the suit property sold the same to the defendant, Abdul Jabbar, predecessor of the petitioners by a registered deed dated 15-12-1985 and delivered possession of the same. After purchase the said Abdul Jabbar got his name mutated in the khatian and have been in possession by giving boundary wall and barb wire fencing, the story of inclusion of the property in the deed of the plaintiff is false, baseless and fraudulently created for filing of this suit.

4. The trial court framed four issues for determination of the dispute. In course of hearing the plaintiff examined six witnesses as PWs and submitted documents in favour of her case. The defendant examined two witnesses as DWs and submitted some documents in favour of their case which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court upon contested hearing dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 25-9-1991.

5. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial court the plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No. 701 of 1991 before the District Judge, Chittagong. Eventually, the said appeal was heard by the Joint District Judge and Second Commercial Court, Chittagong on transfer who after contested hearing allowed the appeal and sent the case on remand directing the trial court to allow both the parties to amend their plaint and written statement.

6. At this stage the defendant-respondent-petitioner moved this Court by filing this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay.

7. Mr Kamal ul Alam, Senior Advocate with Mr Md Masud Alam, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submit that admittedly, the suit land belonged to Nawab Ali. The said Nawab Ali on the same date executed and registered two deeds of gift, one in favour of the plaintiff as his second wife and another in favour of his son Md Muslim, a son by another wife. In the schedule of both the deeds of gift the suit property covered by RS plot No. 172 measuring 21 sataks have been included. Subsequently, Md Muslim by a sale deed dated 15-12-185 sold 91 /2 sataks land to Abdul Jabbar, the predecessor of the present petitioners and delivered possession of the same to him. He further submits that while Abdul Jabber was in possession of the suit land all of a sudden the predecessor of the present opposite party, Salema Khatun claiming the property to be her gifted property instituted the instant suit for declaration of title by way of gift and adverse possession.

8. Mr Alam further submits that the question has arisen between the two deeds of gift as to which one shall prevail as per provision of law. Referring to the evidences in respect of both the gift (exhibits-2 and exhibit-A) adduced by the plaintiff in suit, he submits that the plaintiff in his deposition clearly stated that the deed of gift (exhibit-A) was written and executed in the house of the plaintiff and the deed of gift (exhibit 2) written and executed in the registry office which proved that the deed of gift executed in favour of Muslim was earlier one and registration of the same also made before the deed of gift of the plaintiff as appeared from time of registration and serial number of the deed. As such, as per provision of Section 47 of the Registration Act the deed of gift No. 4073 dated 7-6-1969 shall prevail over the deed of gift executed in favour of the plaintiff. He further submits that the plaintiff in suit failed to prove her case by any evidence that after making gift in her favour she got delivery of possession and subsequent record of right stands prepared in her name and she paid rent to the government. But on the other hand the petitioner as defendant adduced evidence in favour of his possession in the suit land, submitted B.S khatian in his vendor's name, got his name mutated in khatian and rent receipts showing payment of rent to the government.

9. He further submits that the PWs examined on behalf of the plaintiff could not prove possession in the suit land, on the other hand the defendant by evidences both oral and documentary successfully proved that they are in possession since their purchase from Md Muslim. He further submits that the trial court while dismissing the suit categorically found that the plaintiff failed to prove that the suit land was mistakenly included in the deed of gift made in favour of defendant No. 8, Md Muslim. And the courts below also found that no specific averments made in the plaint and evidence adduced by the plaintiff in respect of adverse possession and in the absence of such averments in the plaint as well as evidence the trial court felt it unnecessary to frame any issue on the point of title by adverse possession. It is also argued that the trial court though exhaustively discussed all the evidences adduced before it and made observations on the evidence and point of law, the appellate court without adverting and appreciating the observations and findings of the trial court most illegally remanded the suit to the trial court.

10. He argued that the appellate court before sending the case on remand ought to have reversed the findings of the trial court on every point and if feels that there has been non-reading and non-appreciation of evidence and point of law or insufficiency of finding and observation, may send the case on remand for rehearing. But in the present case the appellate court made observation on the point which has already been decided by the trial court giving specific findings, therefore, there was no earthly reason for the appellate court to send the case on remand. It is also argued that had there been any lack of discussion or findings of the trial court on any point or evidence, it was incumbent upon the appellate court to decide the same on appeal instead of sending the case on remand. He further submits that the observations as made by the appellate court for sending the case on remand required no additional evidence to be recorded for disposal of the suit again by the trial court and where no further evidence is required to decide the case again, remand order is not at all justified. As such, the judgment and decree of the appellate court is liable to be set aside. In support of his submissions he has referred to a catena of cases Abdul Motalib vs Iman Ali Mollah reported in 42 DLR (AD) 123, Rafiqul Islam vs. Mir Abdul Ali reported in 44 DLR (AD) 176, Haji Mustafizur Rahman being dead his heirs Kabir Ahmed vs Abdul Kader being dead his heirs Nurul Islam reported in 4 MLR (AD) 1 = 3 BLC (AD) 38, Mrs Zakia Chowdhury vs Abdul Hamid reported in 12 BLT (AD) 136, Khairunnessa vs. Atar Banu reported in 10 BLC (AD) 25, Md Nasir Hosssain Khan vs Md Mujal Mollah being dead his heirs Shahida Begum reported in 7 BLT (AD) 7, Golam Rahman vs Hazera Khatun reported in 47 DLR (AD) 108 and Hedayetullah vs Foyjun Nessa Begum reported in 18 BLC (AD) 139.

11. Heard the learned Advocates for the petitioners, have gone through the revisional application, evidences both oral and documentary lying in lower court records and the impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below.

12. Admittedly, the suit property in question belonged to Nawab Ali who purchased the same from one Abdul Hoque by a register deed dated 27-1-1964. Said Nawab Ali executed two deeds of gift dated 7-6-1969 and registered on 8-7-1969 bearing Nos. 4073 and 4080 in favour of his son, Md Muslim and his second wife Salema Khatun respectively.

13. The deed of gift bearing No. 4073 was made by Nawab Ali in favour of his son Md Muslim in respect of suit property along with other non-suited property. Deed of gift No. 4080 in favour of plaintiff, Salema Khatun was for suit property only. The suit property covered by RS plot No. 172 measuring 47 sataks land in total. As per plaint case 26 sataks of land was acquired by the government from Abdul Hoque. Nawab Ali purchased remaining 21 sataks of land from Abdul Hoque and the same was gifted by the aforesaid two deeds of gift in favour of wife of Nawab Ali and his son Md Muslim. Now the question has arisen, between the two deeds of gift for the same property which one shall prevail. The trial court in its judgment considered both the deeds of gift and considering evidences adduced by the plaintiff and the provisions of law held that:

“বাদীনির পি ডব্লিউ-১ এর জেরায় স্বীকার করে যে, ৮নং বিবাদী মুসলিমের দানপত্র বাদীনীর ঘরে লেখা হইয়াছে আর  বাদীনীর দানপত্র রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসে লিখা হয় এবং রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসেই নোয়াব আলী বাদীনির দানপত্র সম্পাদন করিয়াছে। দানপত্র সম্পাদনের পর বাদীনি রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসে দলিল দাখিল করিয়াছে। বাদীনীর উক্ত স্বীকারোক্তি দ্বারা এই অর্থ দীড়ায় যে, যেদিন বাদীনির বরাবরীয় কবলা সম্পাদন হয় সেইদিনই যদি বাদিনি রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসে দানপত্র দাখিল করে তা হইলে দেখা যায় যে, কবলা রেজিষ্ট্রি হইয়াছে এবং দাখিল হইয়াছে ৮-৭-৬৯ ইং তাং আর কবলা লেখা-পড়া-সম্পাদনও হইয়াছে ৮-৭-৬৯ ইং তারিখে কারণ [Exhibit-2 দৃষ্টে তাহাই পরিলক্ষিত হয়। আর অবস্থা যদি তাহাই হয় তা হইলে বাদীনির বরাবরীয় কবলাটির সঠিকতা সম্পর্কে বিবাদীদের অভিযোগটিই সত্য । এবং বাদীনি যে, ৮-৭-৬৯ ইং তাং লেখকের যোগাযোগে অনেক দলিল রেজিস্ট্রির সুবিধা গ্রহণ করিয়া নোয়াব আলী মিয়ার অগোচরে অলক্ষ্যে স্বাক্ষর গ্রহণ করিয়াছে এবং উক্ত কবলার পূর্বের তারিখে ষ্ট্যাম্প খরিদ করিয়া পূর্বের তারিখ দেখাইয়া সম্পাদনের কাটি সম্পাদন করিয়াছে তাহাই প্রমাণিত হয়। মূলতঃ স্বীকৃত মতেই মুসলিমের বরাবরীয় ৭-৬-৬৯ ইং তাং সম্পাদিত দানপত্রটি বাদীনির ঘরে লেখা হইয়া ও সম্পাদিত হইয়া থাকিলে বাদীনির বরাবরীয় কবলাটিও বাদীনির ঘরে লেখা-পড়া ও সম্পাদন হওয়ার কথা কিন্তু রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসে লেখা ও সম্পাদনের কাজ হইয়া থাকিবে কেন? বাদীনির দাখিলীয় নোয়াব আলীর এক্টেটের সেরেস্তার খাতা [Ext.1] এর ৭৭ পৃষ্ঠার মন্তব্যে দেখা যায় ��ে, নালিশী আর এস ১৯৯, ২০২ দাগ নোয়াব আলীর স্ত্রী জোহরা বেগমের নামে লেখা । আর এস ২১১, ২১২ দাগের সমুদয় জমি, নোয়াব আলীর স্ত্রী জোহরা খানমের নামে এবং নালিশী আর এস ১৭২ দাগের ২১ শতক জমি বাদীনি সলেমা খাতুনের নামে লেখা। প্রশ্ন হইল, যেখানে আর এস ২০২/২১১/১৯৯ দাগের সম্পূর্ণ খরিদা (নোয়াব আলীর) জমি নোয়াব আলী ৭-৬-৬৯ ইং তাং দানপত্র Ext.A মূলে ৮নং বিবাদী মুসলিমকে দান করার বিষয়টি বাদীনি কর্তৃক স্বীকৃত এবং উক্ত জমি যেহেতু বাদীনি ছাড়া কেহ দাবী করে না সেক্ষেত্রে জমি Ext.1 এর ডাইরীর ৭৭ পৃষ্ঠায় মন্তব্য কলামে জাহানারাও জোহরা নামে লেখা থাকিবে কেন? উক্ত লেখার কারণে নাঃ জমির বিষয়ে বাদীনির নামে লিখিত মন্তব্য বিশ্বাস করিলে তো জাহানারাও জোহ্রারা নামে লিখিত ২০২/২১১/২১২/১৯৯ দাগের জমির স্বত্ব দখলকেও বিশ্বাস করিতে হইবে । সুতরাং Ext.1 এর ৭৭ পৃষ্ঠায় মন্তব্য কলাম লিখার বিষয়টি বাদীর বরাবরে নাঃ জমি দান করার ক্ষেত্রে গ্রহণ যোগ্য সাক্ষ্য বলিয়া আদালত মনে করেন  না। তাছাড়া বাদীনির বরাবরীয় দানপত্র পরে রেজিস্ট্রি অফিসে উত্থাপিত এবং রেজিস্ট্রি হয় এবং মুর্সলিমের বরাবরে কবলা বাদীনির কবলার পূর্বে উথথাপিত হয় ও রেজিস্ট্রি হয় সে কারণে বাদীনির চেয়ে মুসলিম এর দানপত্রটি আইনগত গুরুত্ব বেশি । উক্ত রেজিস্ট্রি কবলার আভ্যন্তরীণ বক্তব্য বা এবারতনামার (Everment) বিপরীতে বাদীনি কোন মৌখিক সাক্ষীর মাধ্যমে আপত্তি উত্থাপন করিবার অধিকারী নহে। এক্ষেত্রে বাদীনি সাক্ষ্য আইনের ৯১ ধারার বিধান মোতাবেক বারিত এবং উক্ত আইনের ৯২ ধারার কোন সুবিধাও অত্র মামলার ক্ষেত্রে বাদীনি পাওয়ার অধিকারী নহে।”

14. From the above observations of the trial court it appears that the trial court considering all the evidences and circumstances held that the deed of gift made by Nawab Ali in favour of his son Md Muslim is earlier one and as per section 47 of the Registration Act the deed of gift (exhibit-A) in favour of Md Muslim was executed earlier and shall prevail over the deed of gift executed in favour of plaintiff, Salema Khatun.

15. The trial court in respect of possession of the suit land held that the plaintiff though in her evidence claimed that she has been possessing the suit land since her gift, but could not produce any paper or record of right or any rent receipts showing payment of rent to the government.

16. On the other hand the defendant by oral evidence and by submitting BS khatian in the name of his vendor, rent receipts showing payment of rent and the mutation khatian standing in his name could prove that the defendant is in possession of the suit land measuring 9½ sataks and observed that plaintiff has failed to establish her title by way of gift and adverse possession.

17. From perusal of the plaint in suit, it appears that the plaintiff though made a prayer of acquiring title by adverse possession but no specific averment or statement have been made in the plaint and evidences led to that effect.

Moreover, a plaintiff cannot seek a declaration of title on the basis of document and by way of adverse possession at the same time. The trial court in its judgment discussed all the evidences and the exhibits and independently given findings on each point of law and considering all the aspects came to a definite finding that the claim of the plaintiff to the effect that the suit property was wrongly included in the deed of gift No. 4073 in the name of Md Muslim is not at all believable. In weighing the evidences in respect of making gift in favour of the plaintiff the trial court held that;

“মুসলিম আইনানুযায়ী দানের প্রধান শর্ত হইল প্রস্তাব, গ্রহণও দখল অর্পণ বা (offer, acceptance and delivery of possession) । যেহেতু বাদী ৮নং বিবাদীর এবং দাতা নোয়াব আলীর মধ্যে Ext.A, Ext.2 দ্বারা অফার গ্রহণ (acceptance) উপাদান গুলি পরিলক্ষিত হয় তাই বাস্তবিক পক্ষে নাঃ জমির দখল যে প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছে তাহার বরাবরেই দানও সঠিক ও আইন সম্মত হইয়াছে বলিয়া আদালত বিবেচনা করিবেন।

এখানে বাদী না জমির স্বত্ব দখল করিয়া অত্র মামলা আনায়ন করিয়াছে । অত্র মামলায় ৮নং বিবাদী অনুপস্থিত । সুতরাং মামলার পারিপার্থিকতা এবং আইনানুযায়ী বাদীনিকেই তাহার বরাবর দানপত্রটি যথার্থতা প্রমাণ করিতে হইবে। নাঃ জমির দখলের ক্ষেত্রে বাদীপক্ষের কৌশলী যুক্তি উথাপন করিয়া বলেন যে, স্বামী যদি তাহার স্ত্রীকে কোন জমি দান করেন সে ক্ষেত্রে দানপত্র দলিলে দখল অর্পণের কথা উল্লেখ থাকিলেই চলিবে (physically) স্ত্রীকে বাস্তবিক ভাবে দখল দেওয়ার প্রয়োজন নাই। অবশ্য এই নীতিটি নাবালক পুত্রের ক্ষেত্রে পিতা কর্তৃক দানপত্র করার ক্ষেত্রেও কার্ধকর। বাদীনি স্বীকার করিয়াছে যে, ৮নং বিবাদী ৮-৭-৬৯ তাং নাবালক ছিল। সুতরাং উক্ত নীতিটি বাদীনি এবং ৮নং বিবাদী নোয়াব আলী থেকে দখল প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছে তাহা নির্ধারণ করিয়া দেখিতে হইবে । মূলতঃ নাঃ জমি যে নোয়াব আলী মিয়া বাদীনিকে দখল দিয়াছে সেরূপ কোন দাবী বাদীনি পি ডব্লিউ-১ জবান বন্দিতে দাবী করে নাই। তাছাড়া বাদীনির অন্য সাক্ষী পি ডব্লিউ-২, পি ডব্লিউ-৩, পিডবিউ-৪, পি ডব্লিউ-৫, পিডব্লিউ -৬ কেহই তাহাদের জবান বন্দিতে দাবী করে নাই যে, নালিশী জমি দান করিয়া নোয়াব আলী মিয়া বাদীনিকে নাঃ জমি দখল বুঝাইয়া দিয়াছে। মূলতঃ পি ডব্লিউ-৬ হাজী আউয়ুব আলী তাহার সাক্ষ্যে বলেন যে, দান করার ১ বৎসর পর নাঃ জমি নোয়াব আলী বাদীনিকে দখল দিয়াছে। মূলতঃ দানের প্রধান শর্ত হইল যে, দাতা দানের ইচ্ছা প্রকাশ করিবে গ্রহীতা উক্ত ইচ্ছা বা প্রস্তাব গ্রহণ করিবে এবং দাতা তৎক্ষণাতই দানের বিষয় বন্ধু গ্রহীতাকে বুঝাইয়া দিবে । তাছাড়া বাদীনি যে নাঃ জমি ১৯৬৯ ইং সন হইতে নাঃ জমিতে দখলে ছিল সেরূপ কার্ষ্য প্রমাণে বাদীনি কোন কাগজপত্র আদালতে দাখিল করে নাই। নালিশী জমিতে বাদীনি দখল করার প্রমাণে কোন ঘটনা বা কার্যে্র প্রমাণ করিতে পারে নাই।”

18. The trial court while dismissing the suit left no evidence both oral and documentary untouched and undicussed, but the appellate court while allowing the appeal and remanding the suit for rehearing though rightly observed that the plaintiff did not pray for cancellation of the deed or declaring the deed of gift executed in favour of defendant No. 8, Mulsim has not been acted upon in respect of the suit land and did not claim that the khatian has been wrongly recorded in the name of Muslim but wrongly observed that the trial court failed to give decision and findings on each issue framed by the court and also held that the court below failed to frame issue on adverse possession and give any finding on that issue. But in fact the plaintiff has no case of adverse possession in her plaint as well as in the evidences adduced before the court. Therefore, there was no need of framing any issue on adverse possession by the trial court. The appellate court also failed to appreciate the provision of law and held that the trial court only relying on the timing of registration of the deed considered deed of gift of the defendant No. 8, but from the observation of the trial court it appears that the trial court not only considered time of registration of the deed, but also considering the time of execution of both the deeds held that the deed of the defendant No. 8 shall prevail over the deed of the plaintiff.

19. From perusal of the judgment of the appellate court, this Court finds that the observations and findings of the appellate court is contrary to each other and the appellate court failed to give reason for remanding the case to the trial court for rehearing. The point discussed and raised in the judgment of the appellate court show that all those points and questions have been resolved by the trial court in its judgment exhaustively.

<u>20. Section 47 of the Registration Act decides the validity of two kabalas from the same vendor. This section apply when the same vendor successively transfers the same property to different purchasers at different time. The trial court from the evidence of PW 1 found that the deed of defendant No. 8 was executed in the house of the plaintiff and the deed of the plaintiff was executed in the registry office on the same day and the deed of defendant No. 8 bears the number and time of registration prior to the deed of the plaintiff and held that the deed of defendant No. 8 is earlier and it will prevail over the later one. In the case of Rafiqul Islam and Mir Abdul Ali the appellate division held that:</u>

<u>"the sale-deed which was executed earlier but registered later in point of time will prevail over the sale-deed executed later but registered earlier in point of time and the criterion in such cases for the purpose of determining when the sale takes effect is not the date of registration but the date of execution of the sale-deed itself".</u>

<u>21. In view of the above observations this Court finds that the deed of defendant No. 8 not only earlier in point of time of registration, but it was also earlier in point of time of execution. Therefore, the deed of gift made in favour of defendant No. 8 shall prevail over the deed of the plaintiff. The appellate court while allowing the appeal most unfortunately failed to appreciate the provisions of law and also failed to observe on what point the suit was required to be sent on remand. On perusal of the judgment of the trial court it appears that it has considered the evidence on record and dismissed the suit, but the appellate court below without reversing the findings given by the trial court remanded the suit to the court below for rehearing. The evidences on record are seems to be sufficient to dispose of the case by the appellate court. Therefore, this Court feels that it should not be remanded by the appellate court where the trial court dismissed the suit considering all the evidences on records both oral and documentary only to fill up the lacuna of the plaintiff.</u>

22. In view of the above, I find that the trial court rightly dismissed the suit and the appellate court wrongly decided the matter in dispute sending the suit on remand for rehearing.

23. Taking into consideration the above, this Court finds merit in the Rule as well as submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner.

24. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, without any order as to costs.

25. The judgment and decree dated 6-4-2002 passed by the Joint District Judge and second Commercial Court, Chittagong in Other Appeal No. 701 of 1991 allowing the appeal and sending the suit on remand for rehearing is hereby set aside and the judgment of the trial court is hereby restored.

26. The Order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned and send down the lower court records at once.

End.

Kamal ul Alam, Senior Advocate --------- For the Respondant No. 1. 
Anik R. Haque ------ For the Auction-Purchaser.

full_judgment:
By filing this application, the plaintiff (Judgment-Debtor) is praying for recalling the Order dated 13-8-2018 passed by this Court confirming auction-sale of the coastal tanker 'MT Asha' held on 20-3-2018 and for accepting an amount of Taka 39,38,372 under Payment Order No.0946692/215 dated 22-9-2018 in satisfaction of the decreetal amount in Admiralty Suit No. 05 of 2002 with a further amount of Taka 4,59,500 as solatium vide Pay Order No. 1002200/215 dated 3-2-2019 made out in the name of the auction-purchaser.

2. Succinctly, the background facts of filing the instant application is that the Plaintiff-Judgment Debtor (hereinafter, "the plaintiff") filed Admiralty Suit No. 05 of 2002 for realization of Taka 31,81,709.80 along with interest @ 18% as freight bills against the principal defendants of the suit. The defendant No. 1 (Jamuna Oil Company Ltd) contested the suit by filing written statement on 7-8-2002, denying the material allegations of the plaint, and making a counter-claim of Taka 39,38,371.47 alleging short landing of its cargo by the plaintiff. The said Admiralty Suit No. 5 of 2002 was dismissed for default on 18-3-2010. By the Judgment and Order dated 10-3-2011, the counter-claim of the defendant No. 1 was decreed in favour of the defendant No. 1 and against the plaintiff for an amount of Taka 39,38,371.47 and, against the said Judgment and Order, the plaintiff filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1819 of 2011, which was dismissed by the Hon'ble Appellate Division by its Judgment and Order dated 15-11-2015. Against the aforesaid Judgment dated 15-11-2015, the plaintiff filed Civil Review Petition No. 173 of 2016, which was pending before the Hon'ble Appellate Division at the time of filing the instant application and, subsequently, it has been dismissed for default (non-appearance) on 15-11-2018. Meanwhile, the defendant No. 1 as decree-holder filed the instant Execution Case No.2 of 2013, and had the coastal tanker 'MT Asha' attached for sale through auction. The plaintiff filed an application on 23-10-2017 praying for stay of the auction-sale along with an account-payee cheque for an amount of Tk. 39,38,372 equivalent to the decreetal amount. Upon hearing the application, this Court passed an Order dated 23-10-2017 staying the auction proceedings and, upon considering the ill health of the Managing Director of the plaintiff-company, allowed until 23-2-2018 for encashment of the said cheque, ordering that otherwise a proceeding shall be caused under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881(shortly, NI Act). As the plaintiff was unable to arrange for encashment of the cheque, this Court by Order dated 27-2-2018 asked the plaintiff to show cause as to why a proceeding under the NI Act shall not be initiated against it, and further vacated the Order of stay on auction proceedings and directed the Marshall to take steps for auction-sale of the vessel. The auction notice was published on 10-3-2018, and the auction was held on 20-3-2018. On the day of the auction i.e. 20-3-2018, the auction-purchaser, Al-Haj Abul Kalam Azad (Babul), Proprietor M/s Padma Ship Recycling Industries, bid an amount of Taka 1,05,70,700, which was the highest bid for the vessel, submitting a Pay Order of 10% of the bid-money as earnest money. Against the Order dated 20-3-2018 holding the auction, the plaintiff filed CMP No. 361 of 2018, along with a Bank Guarantee for the decreetal amount, and the Hon'ble Judge-in-Chambers was pleased to pass an Order dated 27-3-2018 staying the auction and directed for the Bank Guarantee to be kept with the Registrar General of the Supreme Court, where it remains till date unencashed. The ensuing Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2573 of 2018, however, was dismissed by Order dated 7-8-2018. Thereafter, the auction-sale was confirmed by this Court's Order dated 13-8-2018. Now, when an application by the auction-purchaser for a direction to deliver the vessel is pending before this Court, the plaintiff has come up with this application praying for recalling this Court's above-mentioned Order dated 13-8-2018, upon depositing two separate Pay Orders, one for satisfaction of the decreetal amount and another in the name of the auction-purchaser as solatium.

3. The auction-purchaser is contesting this application by filing written objection contending, inter-alia, that the Judgment-Debtor (plaintiff) having exhausted all the stages in the suit and, thereafter, again all the stages in the execution case, now has come up with this device with a malafide intention to abuse the process of this Court and simply attempting to harass this bonafide auction-purchaser. The auction held on 20-3-2018 was a continuation of the auction process that was initiated by publication of auction notices 1st time on 17-10-2017. The Judgment-Debtor, including his counsel in person, has made several representations or promises to this Court for paying off the decreetal amount, but ultimately it proved that the Judgment-Debtor persistently flouted with the Court proceedings and obtained unfair advantage to delay the process of execution. It is stated that the Judgment-Debtor obtained stay of the auction 1st time on 23-10-2017 by misleading this Court with a cheque for paying the decreetal amount, but the cheque was dishonored. The Judgment-Debtor also misled the Hon'ble Appellate Division by presenting a Bank Guarantee which was encashable after 6 (six) months and also presenting blank cheque instead of Pay Order as per the direction of the Court, which the Appellate Division refused to accept.

4. Mr Mustafizur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the Judgment-Debtor contends that there has been serious illegalities in calling and holding the auction for selling the vessel inasmuch as the auction-sale was held on 20-3-2018, while the notice for such auction-sale was given only on 10-3-2018; that is to say, there was only 10 (ten) days between the notice and the auction. By taking me through Order 21 Rule 68 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC), he submits that in the case of property of the kind described in the Proviso to Order XXI, rule 43 of the CPC, no sale in execution shall, without the consent in writing of the Judgment-Debtor, take place until after the expiration of at least 30 (thirty) days in the case of immovable property, and of at least 15 (fifteen) days in the case of movable property, calculated from the date on which the copy of the proclamation has been affixed on the Court-house of the Judge ordering the sale and the proclamation has to be in the form prescribed under Order XXI, rule 66 of the CPC. He submits that the Proviso of Order XXI, rule 43 of the CPC is inapplicable in the instant case in that the said provision concerns goods which are subject to speedy and natural decay or when the expense of keeping it in custody is likely to exceed its value. In an effort to elaborate his above submissions, he contends that in the instant case, the first proclamation that approximates the requirement of Order XXI, rule 66 of the CPC was not published until 10-3-2018 and, hence, the property intended to be sold being a movable property, the auction-sale ought not to have occurred until 25-3-2018. He submits that the requirement under Order XXI, rule 68 of the CPC is a substantive requirement of law, as opposed to a procedural one, in view of the provision of Order XXI, rule 69(3) of the CPC, which provides that every sale shall be stopped if, before the lot is knocked down, the debt and costs includir3 the costs of the sale, are tendered to the officer conducting sale, or proof is given to his satisfaction that the amount of such debt and costs have been paid into Court which ordered the sale. According to Mr Khan, Order XXI, rule 69(3) of the CPC gives an opportunity to the Judgment-Debtor to pay off the decreetal amount along with costs, even after the proclamation of sale of 15 (fifteen) days in case of a movable property, before any auction takes place, unless the Judgment-Debtor has consented to a shorter period under Order 21 Rule 68 of the CPC. He argues that since in the instant case, the plaintiff had never consented to a shorter period under Order XXI, rule 68 of the CPC, the auction suffers from an illegality for violating the said provisions of Order XXI, rule 68 of the CPC, which is to the prejudice of the rights to property of the plaintiff. Mr Khan forcefully submits that this is a serious illegality, which cannot be regarded as a procedural irregularity within the terms of Order XXI, rule 78 of the CPC not vitiating the sale. In an effort to buttress up his argument on this issue, he refers to the case of Narayan Chandra vs Manhar Mandal 43 DLR (AD) 152 and submits that on the ground of non-compliance of these provisions the Appellate Division set aside the auction-sale held in the afore-cited case.

5. He, then, alleges that as per the plaintiff's claim, the market value of the vessel is about 20 (twenty) crore, but the vessel has been sold in auction only at I (one) crore and odds. He contends that it was the duty of the concerned officials of the Admiralty section of this Court to either appoint a valuer for assessment of the value of the vessel or to take information from the market by appointing a surveyor regarding the price and, then, place the same to the Hon'ble Presiding Judge of the Admiralty Court, and had the value of the vessel been assessed before inviting the auction, the Hon'ble Presiding Judge would not have agreed to accept the bid at such a low price.

6. Mr Khan next alleges that the plaintiff has deposited a Bank Guarantee of the decreetal amount before the Hon'ble Appellate Division on 27-3-2018 which is kept under the safe custody of the Registrar General, who is the Marshall of this Court, and till date it remains uncashed. But this information was not disclosed to the Hon'ble Presiding Judge of the Admiralty Court at the time of filing the application for confirmation of auction-sale on 13-8-2018. He contends that had this information been placed before the Hon'ble Presiding Judge on 13-8-2018, the auction-sale would not have been confirmed by the Hon'ble Presiding Judge. He argues that because of obtaining this confirmation Order, the auction-purchaser is now taking recourse to the relevant provisions of the CPC to defeat the plaintiff's right.

7. He makes a humble prayer before this Court to apply the principles of equity in this case, pointing out to a number incidents took place in this suit; such as (i) the plaintiff's suit was not professionally conducted by the filing lawyer, for, the suit was, at first, dismissed for default and, thereafter, it was not restored, (ii) the defendant's counter-claim was decreed exparte simply on the findings that there was a short delivery of only 1,49,746 liters of diesel out of 1866.56 Metric Tons and (iii) the auction was held without obtaining any valuation of the vessel. He argues that had the plaintiff been able to produce his witnesses (PWs), there was a fair chance to establish his case that it was the concerned staffs of the defendant No. 1 who were liable for the short delivery. By referring to the case of Denim Attires Ltd vs Iffat Obaid reported in 2019 ALR (AD) Online 107 (CP No. 2592 of 2017, Judgment delivered on 11-3-2018), he submits that the Hon'ble Appellate Division granted equitable relief in the cited case, even after the property was delivered to the auction-purchaser by executing the registered deed of sale following the auction-sale.

8. Per contra, Mr Anik R. Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the auction-purchaser submits that the Hon'ble Appellate Division has affirmed both the original Judgments and Decree and the auction-sale in the execution case, and the Appellate Division having not found any legal infirmity in the Orders passed by the High Court Division upheld the auction-sale on both the occasions. By placing the provisions of Order 21 Rule 77(2) of the CPC, Mr Haque submits that upon payment of the purchase-money, the auction-sale has been finalized and the sale has become absolute and the auction-purchaser has acquired the legal title in the property which cannot be taken away or circumvented. He submits that it is now an obligation for the executing Court to deliver the moveable property to the auction-purchaser under Order 21 Rule 79 of the CPC. By referring to the case of Fariduddin Chowdhury vs Sylhet Gas Works Ltd 1995 BLT (AD) 168 and the case of Sonali Bank vs Artharin Adalat 15 MLR (AD) 20 = 62 DLR (AD) 20: Mr Haque submits that once the auction is completed, no relief is available against such auction-sale, as there is no provision in any law or in Order XXI, of the CPC to set aside a confirmation of sale in case of moveable property. He submits that once the sale is confirmed and made absolute, the Judgment-Debtor losses his right to receive back the property in question even on satisfying the decreetal amount. He argues that if the confirmation of sale is set aside in the present case, it will tantamount to declaring the title of the auction-purchaser nugatory, thereby, extending and giving an unwarranted benevolence to the Judgment-Debtor.

9. He submits that the auction-sale was conducted as per the law in compliance with Order XXI, rule 68 of the CPC. He further submits that the specification of time in Order XXI, rule 68 of the CPC is merely a procedural law, which is confirmed by Order XXI, rule 78 of the CPC which provides that an auction-sale concerning a moveable property will not be vitiated due to an irregularity and, thus, it is open to the Judgment-Debtor to institute suit against the person responsible for the irregularity, if any, in conducting the auction-sale provided the Judgment-Debtor has sustained an injury. He contends that, in this case, the Judgment-Debtor will not be able to show that it has sustained an injury owing to such irregularity, because the Judgment-Debtor has been avoiding to pay the decreetal amount in the last 6 (six) years by abusing the process of the Court.

10. Mr Haque lastly submits that in view of the dubious conduct of the Judgment-Debtor in an effort to frustrate the execution of the decree, it is clear that he has not come in clean hands before this Court and, as such, he is not entitled to plea for equitable relief.

11. One day the plaintiff (Judgment-Debtor) having appeared in person in the Court-room was telling so many stories by wailing and lamentation regarding this suit and prayed for not to dispose of the application summarily. Pursuant thereto, this Court assured him that the Court would take his statements into consideration by examining all the relevant papers, Order-sheets and the applicable laws.

<u>12. Upon hearing the learned Advocate for the auction-purchaser and the learned Advocate for the Judgment-Debtor (plaintiff), perusing the Judgment and Decree (ex parte) dated 10-3-2011 passed by the Admiralty Court in the Admiralty Suit No.5 of 2002, the Judgment and Order dated 15-11-2015 passed by the Appellate Division in the CP No. 1819 of 2011, which was preferred against the aforesaid Judgment and Decree dated 10-3-2011, the entire Order-sheets of the suit as well as the execution case and examining the all the provisions of Order XXI of the CPC together with relevant case-laws, it appears to this Court that there is hardly any scope for this Court to recall the Order dated 13-8-2018 by which the auction was confirmed inasmuch as this Court, upon exhausting all the formalities for execution of the decree, has eventually confirmed the auction-sale of the coastal tanker MT ASHA held on 20-3-2018. It is the settled law of this jurisdiction that once the auction-sale is confirmed by the executing Court upon being satisfied that the auction-purchaser has complied with the Directions and Orders issued/passed by the executing Court from time to time, including the payment of the consideration money within the stipulated time, then there is no scope for the executing Court to show any sympathy to the Judgment-Debtor even if the Judgment-Debtor pays full decreetal amount together with a further amount of solatium after confirmation of auction-sale. In this case, it is apparent that after confirmation of auction-sale the Judgment-Debtor (plaintiff), having managed the funds, has deposited a Pay Order of the decreetal amount together with a Pay Order for an amount of Taka 4,59,500 as solatium vide Pay Order No. 1002200/215 dated 3-2-2019, however, this Court is unable to exercise its discretion at this stage. While it is evident from the record that this suit was dealt with by his previous engaged lawyer in a very cavalier fashion, there is no provision in the law to help the plaintiff at the fag end of the execution of a lawful decree. This Court has taken note of the facts that (i) the original suit was dismissed for default, but the engaged lawyer of that time did not restore the suit within the prescribed time and consequently this plaintiff missed the chance to prove his case by adducing relevant witnesses before the trial Court as to whether the Judgment-Debtor (plaintiff) was responsible for the shortage of delivery or the Jamuna Oil Company (defendant) was liable for the said shortage and (ii) after the suit was dismissed for default, the plaintiff's engaged lawyer again missed the chance to contest the counter-claim and eventually the original suit was decreed exparte. It is worthwhile to note here that the basis of exparte decree is allegation against the plaintiff that he has misappropriated the diesel, but the Hon'ble Appellate Division has not agreed with the said findings, albeit the plaintiff's appeal was dismissed.</u>

13. Be that as it may, from a minute perusal of the Order sheets, it transpires that when the execution case was kicked off, the Judgment-Debtor (plaintiff) was struggling to manage required funds for depositing before the executing Court to meet up the decreetal amount, and for this purpose he was taking time form this Court again and again but ultimately he failed hopelessly. And, eventually, this Court did not have any option other than to confirm the auction-sale. At a belated stage, when the Judgment-Debtor (plaintiff) managed the funds to deposit before this Court against the decreetal amount and also for an amount of solatium, by now, this Court has become powerless to do anything for this Judgment-Debtor (plaintiff).

14. This Court rejects the plaintiff's allegation that the vessel has been sold in auction at a shockingly low price, for, the auction was invited twice through publishing advertisements in the daily newspapers. Although it was incumbent upon the concerned officials of the administrative wing of the Admiralty Court to obtain a valuation report through a surveyor or through the concerned business forum, however, because of not placing the valuation report before the Hon'ble Presiding Judge of the Admiralty Court, it cannot now be hold that the auction-sale has been illegal. But I would record here that it would have been a fairer practice on part of Advocate M. Golam Arshed, who had filed the application for confirmation of auction-sale, had he disclosed the facts of depositing the Bank Guarantee of decreetal amount by the plaintiff before the Hon'ble Appellate Division, which still remains uncashed.

<u>15. The learned Advocate for the Judgment-Debtor (plaintiff) has tried his best to make out a case by referring to the case of Denim Attires Ltd vs Iffat Obaid, reported in 2019 ALR (AD) Online 107 (CP No. 2592 of 2017, Judgment delivered on 11-3-2018) wherein the Hon'ble Appellate Division set aside the auction-sale, even though the auction-purchaser not only had paid off the full amount of bid money but also had got the sale deed registered through the Court. However, it is the opinion of this Court that since the Hon'ble Appellate Division is endowed with the constitutional power to do the complete justice, it is for the Hon'ble Appellate Division to look into the facts and circumstances of this case and consider it accordingly, if this hapless Judgment-Debtor (plaintiff) prefers any appeal against this Order.</u>

End.
