14. In view of discussions, decisions and reasons stated above, I am of the view that the impugned judgment and decree of the court of appeal below suffers from no legal infirmity which calls for no interference by this court in revision. Thus, I find no merit in the Rule.

15. In the result, the Rule is discharged. However, there will be no order as to costs.

16. Let the Lower Court Records along with a copy of the judgment be sent to the court concerned at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mir Md Joynal Abedin, Advocate -------- For the Petitioner. 
Md Khalilur Rahman, Advocate -------- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Chairman Bangladesh Water Development Board --------Petitioners
Vs.
Md Abdur Rahman -------- Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No. I to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 19-8-2001 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Kurigram in Other Appeal No.2 of 2001 affirming the judgment and decree dated 26-9-2000 passed by the Assistant Judge, Sadar, Kurigram in Other Suit No. 35 of 1999 should not be set aside and, or, such other or further order or orders pass as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Opposite Party No. 1 as plaintiff filed Other Suit No. 35 of 1999 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Kurigram impleading the petitioner Nos. 1-4 as defendant Nos. 1-4 and prayed for a decree for declaration that he is entitled to get gratuity, pension and other service benefit as a regular Government employee.

3. The case of the plaintiff is that he joined the then West Pakistan Water and Power Development Board on 15-12-1961 as Regulator Khalashi and on attaining the age of 57 years on 5-1-1996 he retired from service and defendant No.4 issued a letter for treating him as an irregular employee on retirement and the plaintiff has enjoyed all the service benefits as permanent employee while he was in service and it was the duty of defendant No.1 to make the plain- tiff a permanent employee but due to the issuance of a letter dated 5-12-1995 by the defendant No.4 for treating the plaintiff as a temporary employee, the plaintiff suffered serious loss against which he preferred appeal before the concerned authority to which no reply was given and thereafter the plaintiff served two reminders and since the name of Water Development Board was not included in the schedule of Administrative Tribunal, the plaintiff had to institute the present suit for simple declaration.

4. Defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filing joint written statement denying the case of the plaintiff and according to them the suit is not maintainable in its present form and barred by the principle of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence and that Water Development Board is a semi-Government Autonomous Body and the post of the plaintiff is an irregular temporary post.

5. The trial Court decreed the suit.

6. Being aggrieved thereby, the defendants preferred appeal before' the District Judge, Kurigram, which was transferred to the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Kurigram which dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court,

7. Being aggrieved thereby, the defendants as petitioners filed an application under section 115( I) of the Code of Civil Procedure before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

8. Mr Mir Md Joynal Abedin, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the Courts below have committed error of law resulting in an error in 'the decision occasioning failure of justice and erroneously decreed the suit. He next submits that the Courts below wrongly treated the plaintiff as a regular Government employee and accordingly, decreed the suit without considering the Bangladesh Water Development Board is an autonomous semi- Government Organisation and its employees are not Government employees. He also submits that the plaintiff is a casual employee and got temporary appointment to the post of regulator Khalashi, a labour, under the defendants and his grievance can only be adjudicated by the competent Labour Court and not by a Civil Court and, as such; the suit is liable to be dismissed. He next submits that the plaintiff filed a suit for simple declaration and did not pray for any consequential relief and thus the decree which has been passed by the Courts below is not an executable one. The learned Advocate referred an unreported decision, as passed in a Writ Petition and submits that a worker who has been retired would seek redress under the provisions of Payment of Wages Act for realisation of his benefits consequent upon retirement. He submits that if a remedy has been 'provided under any other law, it created an implied bar to a proceeding under the Code of Civil Procedure, before the Civil Court. In support to his contention, the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 30 DLR 219. Lastly, the learned Advocate submits that the suit filed by the plaintiff was not maintainable as the plaintiff was a worker and had remedy before the Labour Court and the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act in the absence of any prayer for consequential relief. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 40 DLR (AD) 45.

9. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, files a counter-affidavit and submits that the plaintiff has succeeded to prove his ,case before the Courts below and considering the facts, circumstance and evidence on record, the trial Court decreed the suit and the lower appellate Court affirmed the judgment passed by the trial Court on the basis of materials on record and there being no error in the decision and moreso, no failure of justice being occasioned to the defendant- petitioners, the Rule is liable to be discharged. He submits that though defendants submitted written statement before the said Court, they did not adduce any witness in support to their written statement for which it can be said that the suit was not contested by the defendants before the Courts below. He points out that in the written statement the defendants did not challenge the claim of the plaintiff that he is a regular employee and the defendants also did not challenge the authority of the Court holding the trial and that the Labour Court only has exclusive jurisdiction to try the grievances of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate referred Exhibit 4 and submits that the plaintiff as Regulator Khalashi joined service on 15-12-1961 and thereafter his service book was opened by the authority as an employee and his pay was fixed as per national pay scale introduced by the Government and he got increment and time-scale from time to time. He also submits that another Regulator Khalashi Md Abdus Sattar by the order dated 23-10-2001 was considered as a regular employee and was given his gratuity benefits. The learned Advocate submits that the defendant being a statutory Corporation, there is no reason to believe that such Corporation will not implement the decision of the Courts. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred a decision as reported in 50 DLR 411. He also submits that suit for negative declaration, under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, is maintainable. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has referred decisions as reported in 40 DLR 226, 37 DLR 49 and 42 DLR 211. He also submits that exclusion of jurisdiction of a Civil Court' should not be readily inferred and the Court shall retain its jurisdiction unless the order passed is without jurisdiction or malafide or not in accordance with Jaw.

10. In support of his contention, the learned Advocate has referred decisions as reported in 43 DLR 407 and 45 DLR 727. He points out that the concurrent findings of the Courts below based on materials on record may not be interfered in the absence of error of law or procedure affecting the merit of the case. In support to his contention the learned Advocate has referred the decisions as reported in 11 MLR 99, 12 MLR (AD) 207.

11. I have heard the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the petitioners and the opposite party and perused the revisional application and the counter-affidavit along with other materials on record. It appears that the plaintiff, who is the present opposite party No. 1 filed Other Suit No. 35 of 1999 against the present petitioners for a declaration that he is entitled to get gratuity, pension and other service benefits being a regular Government employee. The present petitioners as defendants Nos. 1-4 filed written statement but did not adduce any evidence, either oral or documentary, before the Courts below. It appears from Exhibit 4, service book opened by the authority, that the plaintiff opposite party No.1 is an employee and his pay was fixed and he was given increment and time-scale from time to time. Attention of this Court was drawn to the fact that another Regulator Khalashi Md Abdus Sattar, like the present petitioner, after his retirement, was given gratuity and allowances as a regular employee and the present opposite party, even after having judgments in his favour by the Courts below, was not given the gratuity and allowances.

<u>12. It is a settled principle that exclusion of jurisdiction of a Civil Court should not be readily inferred. It is also well settled that even if jurisdiction is so excluded, the Civil Courts have jurisdiction to examine cases whether the provisions of any Act have not been complied with when there is allegation of violation of the rules or procedures, malafide and arbitrariness. Civil Court under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure is competent to entertain a suit and can well investigate the propriety of the order or action complained of as in the present case. Civil Courts always can assume jurisdiction to consider the malafide action of the authority even if there is ouster section or clause of any law made for special purpose. Merely because negative declaration has been sought that can be no ground to hold that the suit does not come within the ambit of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act.</u>

13. It appears that in the written statement no claim was made to the effect that the plaintiff is not an employee and the plaintiffs case should be dismissed being hit by the proviso of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the defendant cannot now on revision be allowed to make out a new case, which he did not make in his written statement. The ground of maintainability needs to be agitated at the earliest possible opportunity, which cannot be done in a belated revisional state, as in the present case. It appears that the facts whether the suit is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and that whether the plaintiff is an employee or not were decided by the Courts below and these findings of facts already arrived by the. Courts below initially, would not be interfered by the revisional Court. The question whether the plaintiff was a worker under the labour law or is an employee of the Board is covered by service rule, which was determined by the Courts below. The defendants did not make any statement in the written statement that the plaintiff is not an employee. Defendant also did not adduce any evidence against the claim of the plaintiff before the Courts below. Retirement is not covered under any of the provisions of any law as grievance and the retirement benefits cannot be claimed by filing complaint case before the Labour Court. In the present case, the plaintiff claiming himself to be an employee of the Board, not being challenged by the defendants before the Courts below filed a suit for declaration before the competent court that he is entitled to get gratuity and other benefits after retirement.

14. The trial Court decreed the suit and the Court of appeal below affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. It appears that the trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court considered all aspects thoroughly and concurrently found that the plaintiff succeeded to prove his case. The decision of both the Courts below, being based on fact, circumstances and evidence on record and there being concurrent findings over the points in issue and there being found no error of law or fact in passing the impugned judgment, I am of the opinion that the impugned judgments and decrees do not warrant any interference by this Court. Since both the Courts below on proper assessment of the evidence on record came to a concurrent finding, this finding is binding upon this Court, unless it is shown that there are misreading or non consideration of material evidence on record in arriving at such finding. The judgments of the Courts below are not tainted with legal infirmity and perversity justifying interference by this Court. After examining the record of the case and hearing the learned Advocates of both the parties, I am of the view that there is sufficient evidence and materials on record to come to the decisions which have been arrived at by the Courts below.

15. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The judgment of the Courts below stand maintained.

Send down the lower Court's record and a Copy of the judgment and order to the Court concerned.

End.

lawyer:
TH Khan with Md Ibrahim Mollah, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
Md Qauyum with JH Afriq, Advocate ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Giasuddin and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Abdul Majid Miah and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule Was issued on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the judgment and decree dated 30-3-1993 and 8-4-1993 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Narayanganj, in Title Appeal No.9 of 1987 affirming the judgment and decree dated 20-12-1987 passed- by the Assistant Judge, Rupganj, Narayanganj, in Title Suit No. 11 of 1986.

2. The facts involved for disposal of the Rule are as follows : The opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 being the plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 11 of 1986 in the Court of Munsif, Rupganj Thana against the petitioners and others for redemption of mortgaged property and for giving delivery of possession of the mortgaged land, asserting, inter alia, that the land measuring 38 decimals comprising plot No. 309 under Khatian No. 256 Mouza Khadn originally belonged to Hossain Baksh who took a loan of Taka 80 from Abdul Jabber and mortgage deed executed on 23-12-1924 and 16-2-1925 and that it was stipulated in the said deed that the mortgagee Abdul Jabber will possess and enjoy the land on account of interest on the money paid and that Hossain Baksh will get the mortgaged land redeemed on payment of the mortgagee money within the month of Falgun, 1334 BS in default, Abdul Jabber will possess the land until the money is paid and that in the event of non payment of money at a time the mortgagee Abdul Jabber Prodhan will be at liberty to realise the money by selling land through the Court. Hossain Baksh died after two years from the date of mortgage, "leaving behind wife Kbadija Bibi, two daughters Aku 'Bibi and Gedi Bibi and one brother, namely, Abdul Karim, and thereafter Khadija Bibi died leaving two daughters as aforesaid and that after the death of Hossain Baksh, his two daughters tried to repay their father's loan to Abdul Jabber but Abdul Jabber being actuated by greed did not accept the money offered and as a result the daughters of Hossain Baksh had not been able to redeem the suit land. Abdul Jabbar died leaving behind four sons and two daughters, the defendant Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 and thereafter son Abdur Rahim died leaving his son, the defendant No. 6 and two daughters, the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 and that the heirs of Hossain Baksh requested the heirs of Abdul Jabbar to return the mortgaged loan on receiving the money put to no effect. Aku Bibi, the daughter of Hossain Baksh, died leaving the plaintiff and the plaintiff requested the defendant Nos. 1-3, the heirs of Abdul Jabber, to release the mortgaged land on acceptance of the money in the 1st part of the month of Ashwin, 1342 BS when the said defendants disclosed that the suit land is in possession of the defendant No.9 and. as such, they have no right to accept the mortgaged money and to deliver possession of the land and that the plaintiff also requested the defendant No. 9 to accept the money and surrender possession of the land but the defendant refused to do so and hence the suit.

3. The defendant No. 9 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the allegations in the plaint and contending, inter alia, that the suit is jarred by limitation and also the suit is barred under the principles of waiver, estoppel and acquiesence and res judicata and further asserted, that the land measuring 30 decimals comprising plot No. 309 belonged to Hossain Mia @ Hossain Baksh and while the said Hossain Baksh had been in possession of the land he needed cash money and, as such, the Said Hossain Baksh mortgaged-the suit land to Abdul Jabber by a registered Mortgage deed (Sud Poshani) dated 12-2-1925 on receiving Taka 80 from the mortgagee and put the mortgagee in possession of the land. It was stipulated in the said (Sud Poshani) mortgage deed that Hossain Baksh will repay the said money to Abdul Jabber within the month of Falgun, 1334 BS and will take back the land and in default, Abdul Jabber will possess and enjoy the land and it was further stipulated that Hossain Baksh will pay rent to the landlord in respect of the suit land and that Hossain Mia @ Hossain Baksh failed to take back the land on payment of the mortgaged money to Abdur Jabber Prodhan within the specified time and that during the lifetime of Hossain Baksh, Hossain Baksh him- self or after his death his legal heirs never tendered the money to Abdur Jabbar or his' heirs in order to redeem the land nor the said Hossain Baksh or his heirs paid rent in respect of the land. Abdur Jabber in order to procure money transferred the suit land to his brother Fenu Prodhan at a, consideration of Taka 80 in the year 1338 BS and the said Fenu Prodhan having acquired the land, has been. in peaceful possession with the knowledge of all concerned including the plaintiff and paid rent to the landlords and after the death of Fenu Prodhan, the contesting defendant and his two sisters became the owner and came into possession of the suit land and that subsequently, the said two sisters transferred their' interest in the land to the defendant by registered sale deed and that during SA operation, the record of rights in respect "Of the' suit land was duly prepared in the name of the defendant and his two sisters and finally published, and that the heirs of Hossain Baksh filed objection against the record of right, vide Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1960 which was rejected on 21-7-1960 and that the defendant and his two sisters mutated their names in the revenue record and paid I rent and enjoyed the land by cultivating the same, with the knowledge of all. The father of defendant and after him the defendant have been in possession of the suit land for the last 62 years and paying rent and that the plaintiff have lost their right, title and interest as the predecessor of the plaintiffs did not get the land redeemed according to the terms of the mortgage deed (Sud Poshani) the predecessor of the plaintiffs never asked the predecessors of the defendants to release the suit land at any point of time,. and that the defendant being the plaintiff instituted a suit for permanent injunction in the Court of Munsif, Rupgonj against the plaintiff being Title Suit No.4 of 1985. The summons of which were duly served upon the plaintiffs but they did not contest the suit and ultimately, the suit was decreed ex parte in favour of the defendant and the plaintiffs being ill advised filed the suit and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Assistant Judge decreed the suit by his Judgment and decree dated 20-12-1986 against which an appeal was preferred before the learned District Judge, Narayanganj which on transfer was heard by the learned Additional District Judge who  dismissed the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 30-3-193.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid Judgment and decree of the appellate Court, the petitioners preferred this revisional application before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr TH Khan, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submitted that the Courts below committed error of law occasioning failure of justice in not holding that the suit for redemption was not maintainable against the contesting defendant, inasmuch as the said defendant was not a mortgagee in respect of the suit land. He further submitted that the Courts below commit- ted errors of law in not considering the long period of possession of about 56 years of the defendants not as a mortgagee or as successor of any mortgagee, but on settlement from the landlord and non-consideration of this vital question that the plaintiffs suit was barred by limitation. The learned Counsel points out that the mortgagor and the heirs of the mortgagor failed to pay rent in respect of the suit land with the result that the land in suit was put in auction and the defendant took settlement from the auction purchaser landlord. The learned Counsel in support of his submission filed some papers like certificate of sale of the suit .land dated 3-8- 1932, amalnama and Dakhila/rent receipt under Order VIIII rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He also submitted that the Court's main function was to adjudicate matters neutrally with proper discovery of facts if possible and. also necessary to ensure justice among the parties and in the instant case, the said documents later discovered by the petitioner, according to him, was very much necessary for proper dispensation of justice and prayed for sending the case back on remand to the trial Court for adjudicating the matter afresh through adducing further evidence as well as amending the pleadings of both the sides, if required. In support of his contention he referred the decision in the. case of Meher Banu vs Abdul Barek reported in 13 BLT (AD) 177.

7. Mr Md Qauyum, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the opposite parties, submitted that the petitioners fought unsuccessfully their case in one footing but by filing some new documents the petitioners tried to present their case absolutely from different footing which the petitioners did not do in either of the Courts below. According to him at this revisional stage no new case can be considered. In course of his argument, the learned Counsel placing before me the Judgments of the Courts below argued that both the Courts below on proper sifting of the evidence of the witnesses and on consideration of all the relevant materials very rightly decreed the suit of the Courts below and committed no error and, as such, at this revisional stage this Court has no jurisdiction in exercise of its revisional power to reverse the concurrent findings of the Courts below. In support of his contention he referred the decision in the case of Abdul Kamal Azad vs Sunhar Ali reported in 46 DLR (AD) 130, Abu Bakkar vs Nazir Ahmed, reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237. But the facts of the instant case are distinguishable from the reported cases.

8. I have perused the Judgments of the Courts below, other materials on record and considered the submissions of the learned Counsels of both the sides.

<u>9. On close reading of the Judgments of the Courts below, it appears to me that both the Courts below passed their Judgments and decrees on the basis of the materials before them and the statement of the PWs and DWs. But the documents, as such, as the certificate dated 3-4-1932, pertaining to the suit land and Dakhilal rent receipt were not placed before the Courts below which the petitioners submitted before this Court with an application under Order VIII, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The documents, however, were discovered' much later then filing of the suit in 1986, but, in my opinion, these documents cannot be thrown out of hand. These documents touching the very basic question of title of the contesting parties are necessary to be examined by the Court for ends of justice and for getting at the truth, overlooking the technicalities. Hence, I feel the case should be sent back on remand to the trial Court for holding a 'fresh trial and I have decided accordingly.</u>

<u>10. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The judgments and decrees of the Courts below are hereby set aside and the case is sent back on remand to the trial Court for holding fresh trial in accordance with law and on the basis of the observation given above quite freely in the interest of justice. Parties are allowed to amend their pleadings and adduce evidence; I should not be understood to have arrived at any finding in the matter.</u>

11. The trial Court is directed to conclude the hearing of the case within 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of this order. Send the lower Court's record at once.

End.

caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 198 of 1976.
lawyer:
Shawkat Ali Khan, Habibur Rahman Khan, Abdul Baset Mazumder, M.L. Bhowmick, A Kashem -----For the Appellants. 
T.H. Khan, Gulfam Shahana Banu, Md, A. Wahab Mia ----For Respondent No. 1.
M. H. Khondker, Nizamuddin Haider, Kazi Siddiqur Rahman -----For Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Madan Mohan Pal Annosatra ----- Appellant.
Vs.
Abdus Samad and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Ranadhir Sen, J.—This appeal at the instance of the defendants 18, 19 and 20 is directed against a judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge in a suit for certain declarations. The plaintiffs Abdus Samad and Chunu Mia jointly Sled Title Suit No. 11 of 1976 praying for the following declaration:-

(a) For decree for declaration of their absolute right title and interest over the suit properties;

(b) For declaration that the S.A. Khatians prepared in the names of the principal defendants are wrong" The properties described in schedule to the plaint are as follows:—

"All that is contained in the property in Mouza Wan sheet No. 2, Ward No. 4 Mahalla Nawabpur, P.S. Sutrapur, District Dacca S.A. Khatian Nos. 53,55 and 56 covering S.A. Plot Nos. 420,422 and 423 measuring 0552, 0396 and 0734 Ajutangsha respectively in holding Nos. 124, 125 and 122 with all buildings and structures thereon corresponding C.S. Khatian Nos. 940, 943 and 941 covering C.S. Plot Nos 19, 21 and 20 measuring 0552, 0734 and 0396 Ajutangsha respectively of Old Mouja Shahar Dacca Sheet No. 49 Ward No. 3, P.S. Kotwali, District Dacca".

The plaintiffs stated the cause of action for the suit in paragraph 11 of the plaint which runs as follows:-

"That the cause of action for this suit has arisen in the last week of May, 1972 when the principal defendants gave out for the first time that their names have been recorded in the S.A. Khatians and threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess from the suit properties at holding Nos. 122, 123, 124 and 124/A, Nawabpur Road, P.S. Sutrapur, District Dacca and within the jurisdiction of this Court."

2. The suit was valued for the purpose of jurisdiction at Tk. 25, 000/00 only and was filed with a fixed court fee of Tk. 20/- only. 2. The suit was contested by some of the defendants of whom defendant No. 18 was one. The contesting defendants variously denied the plaintiff's alleged claim of title and possession and set up title and possession with defendant No. 18. The parties adduced evidence in support of their respective claims. The learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit. Against the judgment and decree defendants 18, 19 and 20 preferred this appeal.

3. Mr. Shawkat Ali Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants pressed the appeal. He took us through the pleadings, relevant facts, circumstances and evidence on record. On behalf of the respondent No. 1 Abdus Samad, Mr. T. H. Khan, the learned Advocate addressed us at certain length. At a later stage Mr. M.H. Khondoker, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 2 Chunnu Mia appeared only for the purpose of mentioning the case for as adjournment and thereafter did not appear to address the Court. However, Mr. Nizamuddin Haider, the learned Advocate appeared for respondent No.2 but did not address the Court on merits of the appeal.4. Mr. T.H. Khan at a certain stage of the hearing of the appeal gave out that he will file an application for withdrawal of the suit with liberty to sue afresh.. The matter was adjourned and on 10th April, 1980 an application for withdrawal of the suit under order 23, rule 1, sub-rule (2) of the Civil Procedure Code was filed stating inter alia that respondent No. 1 Abdus Samad has decided to withdraw from the suit with per-mission to file a fresh suit as "there was formal. defects in the suit." It is not known for what purpose certain statements were made in paragraph 15 which runs as follows: "That it hardly needed exaggeration that much bad blood has been created between your petitioner and Chunnu Mia over properties and various other social and political relations and he is out to harm your petitioner in any way he likes; that as a last resort your petitioner approached for getting all humiliations to give consent to the withdrawal from the suit on 8. 4. 1980 but on 9. 4. 1980 he refused to give consent at the court premises." The prayer was made in the following terms:—

"Therefore it is most humbly prayed that your Lordships may be graciously pleased to allow the petitioner to withdraw from the suit with permission to sue afresh for the ends of justice and /or pass such other or further order or orders as your Lordships may deem fit and proper." On the same day respondent No. 2 Chunnu Mia also filed "an application for per-mission to withdraw the suit." Paragraph 3 of this petition runs as follows:-

"That the plaintiff No. 1 as respondent No. 1 made an oral prayer yesterday before the Hon'ble Court for withdrawal of the suit so far as his claim to his title to the property at 122, Nawabpur Road is concerned. The Hon'ble Court has been pleased to consider the prayer on the undertaking of the learned Advocate for respondent No. 1 to file an application in writing today for the permission to withdraw the suit. In the said circumstances, this plaintiff No. 2 as respondent No, 2 also finds it is difficult for him to proceed with the contest in an appeal and has to make a similar prayer for withdrawal of the suit so far as his property is at 124/A, Nawabpur Road, Dacca with permission to sue fresh." In paragraph 4 respondent No. 2 Chunnu Mia stated :

"That on the claim of the plaintiff respondent No. 1 from the joint plaint instituted by him with the present petitioner, the suit, and for the matter of that decree passed in the suit, automatically becomes non-maintainable, in consequence, the suit also will stand non-maintainable in absence of one of the two joint claimants, although the pointlessness is no longer there, at present."

In paragraph 5 respondent No. 2 made the following statement: That, moreover, the non-co-operation between the two plaintiff respondents has compelled the petitioner to file this application for withdrawal of the suit as barred by non-joinder or absence of plaintiff respondent No. 1 as the necessary party in the suit after withdrawal by plaintiff No. 1"

The prayer was framed in the following terms: "Wherefore it is most humbly prayed that the Hon'ble Court be graciously pleased to permit this plaintiff Respondent No. 2 also to withdraw the suit on ground of formal defect with liberty to sue afresh if not otherwise barred, and to pass such other order or further order or orders as to your Lordships may seem fit and proper."

On behalf of the respondent No. 1 Abdus Samad a supplementary affidavit was filed stating in paragraph 3 what, according to him, were the formal defects in the suit Paragraph 3 of the supplementary affidavit dated 16th April, 1980 runs as follows:-

"That the formal defects are :

(a) the father of the Respondent No 2, the benamder who is still alive, was not made a party in the suit ;

(b) the proper prayer for relief in the suit was not made such as no confirmation of possession was prayed ; (c) the basic documents were not filed at the time of hearing of the suit in the trial Court and thereby the plaintiffs have been let down ;

(d) that there were some procedural defects such as not interrogatory was filed on the pleadings of defect of parties ;

An affidavit-in opposition was filed on behalf of appellant No 1. This affidavit is dated 17th April, 1980. Denying the allegations made in the petition under Order 23 rule 1 (2) C. P. C. dated 10th April, 1980 it was stated in paragraph 14 of the affidavit-in opposition that :-

(e) that through inadvertence wrong number of M.S. No. 158 of 1943 was mentioned in the plaint which was not rectified by amendment :

..It is submitted that what was the formal defect in the suit, nothing has been specifically stated and as such on this ground the respondents are not entitled to have a permission to withdraw their suit. Further on the facts and circumstances and on the conduct of the parties which will be clear from the affidavit and counter affidavit filed in this case, the learned Court should not have exercised discretion in allowing withdrawal of a suit with the permission to sue afresh and in the interest of justice this application is liable to be rejected," An affidavit in reply was filed by respondent No. 1 Abdus Samad who stated in paragraph 12 thereof ; "That with regard to the statements made in paragraph 14 of the affidavit-in-opposition it is respectfully submitted that the term formal defects as envisaged under the provisions of Order XXIII rule 1 of the Code of Civil procedure has a very wide connotation and this Hon'ble Court as a Court of Appeal as well as the Court of first instance has got unfettered power to allow the prayer though no specification of the formal defect given for the ends of justice and the appellants have nothing to oppose ; that, however, the formal defects have been specified in a separate-supplementary affidavit which are not reproduced herein to avoid repetition."

5. The learned Advocates appearing for withdrawal of the suit permission to sue afresh and in opposition thereto address at length. Heard the learned Advocates and perused the petitions, affidavits. Counter-affidavits and affidavit-in reply With reference to the petition dated 10th April 1980 fir withdrawal of the suit, it appears that no case of a formal defect was made out in the petition. The prayer was made for "ends of justice". The learned Advocate, however, sought to improve upon the position by filing a supplementary affidavit dated 16th April, 1980 wherein he indicated the formal defects in paragraph 3 of his petition already quoted. So far as Sub-paragraphs (c), (d) and (e) ate concerned they do not constitute formal defects. In sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) a case of formal defects has been attempted to be made out. In the affidavit-in-opposition appellant No. 1 has seriously challenged both the grounds. According to Mr. Shawkat Ali Khan no case of benamder was ever pleaded or sought to be made out in evidence and there was no issue in that behalf. He has however, referred to some decisions to persuade us to hold a view that the expression "formal defect" should be strictly construed and permission to sue afresh should be refused since the plaintiff respondents have failed to make out a case of formal defects strictly in accordance with law. Mr. T. H. Khan, on the other hand has relied upon the language used in the statute itself which runs as follows:

"Order 23, r. 1;

Withdrawal or abandonment from the claim—

(1) At any time after the institution of a suit the plaintiff may, as against all or any of the defendants, withdraw his suit or abandon part of his claim.

(2)Where the Court is satisfied—

(a) That a suit must fail by reason of some formal defect or

(b) that there are other sufficient grounds for allowing the plaintiff to institute a fresh suit for the subject-matter of a suit or part of a claim. It may, on such terms as it thinks fit, grant the plaintiff permission to withdraw from such suit or abandon such part of a claim with liberty to institute a fresh suit in respect of the subject-matter of such suit or such part of a claim.

(3) Where the plaintiff withdraws from or abandons part of a claim without the permission referred in sub-rule (2), he shall be liable for such costs as the Court may award and shall he precluded from instituting any fresh suit in respect of such subject-matter or such part of the claim.

(4) Nothing in this rule shall be deemed to authorise the Court to permit one of several plaintiffs to withdraw without the consent of the others."

<u>6. Having regard to the provisions of Order 23, rule I, C.P. C. we may examine whether the plaintiff have succeeded in making out a case of formal defect. Views appear to be uniform as regards the power of the Court in this behalf. If the plaintiffs seek to withdraw from the suit, they may do so. No leave of the Court appears to be necessary under Order 23 Rule 1(1) C.P.C. But the liberty or permission whether or not to be given to the plaintiffs to sue afresh in respect of the same subject-matter requires judicial consideration. If the requirements of Order 23 rule 1(2) C.P.C. are satisfied the Court may grant plaintiffs permission to withdraw from the suit with liberty to institute a fresh suit in respect of the subject-matter of such suit. To allow the plaintiffs to withdraw from the suit refusing permission to sue afresh on the same subject-matter does not appear to be in accordance with law. The Court may in appropriate cases reject the application in to. Further the plaintiffs have to satisfy the Court that as a matter of fact, formal defect exists. Having regard to the views noticed above it appears to the interest of justice. Evidently, the object of the rule is not to allow the plaintiffs the opportunity to commence a fresh trial after they have failed to conduct the suit with care and diligence. But the plaintiffs have a right to withdraw from the suit at any stage in terms of the provisions of Order 23, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The expression 'formal defect' has not been defined. It has to be gathered from the pleadings and the facts and circumstances of the case. The decisions referred to by Mr. Shawkat Ali Khan, are distinguishable on facts. We have given our anxious thought to the expression 'formal defect' and in our opinion the expression should not be construed strictly, but must be given liberal meaning to connote a kind of defect which does not affect the merit of the suit. We are supported in our view by the decision of the Dacca High Court in the case of Saidur Rahman Mona and another V. Abdur Rahman and others reported in 13 DLR 106. Reference may also be made in this connection to the Privy Council case of Robert Watson & Co. V. The Collector of Rajshaye & others in 13 Moor's Indian Appeals, 160. In our view the plaintiffs have made out a case of normal defect.</u>

7. For the reasons stated above we allow the plaintiff's prayer for withdrawal of the suit with liberty to institute a fresh suit jointly in respect of the same subject-matter if not other-wise barred.

In the result the impugned judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge are set aside and the appeal is allowed. The plaintiffs prayer for withdrawal of the suit with liberty to institute a fresh suit jointly on the same subject-matter if not otherwise barred, is allowed on condition of payment of a cost of 100 Gold Mohars equivalent to Tk. 1700/-within fifteen days from date with the Deputy Registrar 1 of this Court. In default the prayer for withdrawal of the suit with liberty to sue afresh stands rejected. The appellants may withdraw the amount.

Amirul Islam Chowdhury. J.—I agree.

End.
